World.title: UK fugitive to be extradited – Kubayi
World.content:
PRETORIA - Triple-murder suspect, fugitive Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma, will be extradited to the United Kingdom in the coming days.

The British national, originally from Zimbabwe, was arrested by SAPS and Interpol on Friday after fleeing the UK last week. He is accused of murdering his wife, Zandile, and their two daughters.

Tshuma is due in the Johannesburg Magistrates’ Court on Monday.

Justice Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi confirmed that she would be signing the documents to send Tshuma on his way.

“I firstly wish to commend our SAPS and Interpol for the sterling work that they have done this week in the arrest of Ndodana Mkhanyisi Tshuma, a fugitive wanted for the murder of his wife and two children in the UK.

“According to our movement control systems, he arrived at OR Tambo International Airport on 5 July from Britain.

“Once we received the alert from Interpol, we acted swiftly with a multidisciplinary team conducting tracing and the suspect was arrested in Kensington, Johannesburg.

“At the time he went through OR Tambo, he had not yet been flagged by British authorities. So if he had been flagged, he would not have entered the country.

“He will be extradited to the UK once I have signed all the extradition documents and requests as required by the law in my capacity as Minister of Justice and Constitutional Development. We are informed that the teams are working quite hard and around the clock so that the extradition requests are done and the paperwork is done in time."

World.title: More than 80% of deported foreign nationals are Malawian – Kubayi
World.content:
PRETORIA – The South African government has repatriated 53, 449 foreign nationals and the bulk of that number is made up of Malawian nationals.

Minister Mmamoloko Kubayi revealed this on behalf of the Inter-Ministerial Committee on Migration (IMC) at a briefing on Sunday.

She said the foreign nationals processed for deportation and repatriation were dominated by the Malawians, more than 80%, followed by the Zimbabweans and Mozambicans.

“On 26 June 2026, we reported that 15,162 had been repatriated. We have seen a tremendous increase in the number of foreign nationals who have either been deported or repatriated. To date, a total of 53,449 foreign nationals have been processed for deportation and repatriation,” she said.

Kubayi said the repatriation process has also allowed authorities to nab people who had been evading the police.

“We also wish to report that two suspects who generated a hit during 4 verification (biometrics) at Musina were rearrested: Sheriff Maulana from Malawi was arrested for a murder reported in Chatsworth and Ncube Marshall Vusimuzi from Zimbabwe was wanted for armed robbery and arrested at Point in Durban.

“Similarly, at the Drive-in centre in KwaZulu-Natal, another suspect wanted for rape was nabbed during the verification process. Police have also opened a culpable homicide case after a driver of a bus from Zimbabwe died on the N1 road after the Petros truck stop.

“This bus was not commissioned by the SA government for the record. The case was reported at Musina Police Station. This is the reason why the IMC has insisted that verification must be done without fail.”

Kubayi said an inquest is being conducted into the death of a Malawian national, Kassim Jaffati, who died on his way to Malawi just before the bus reached Beit Bridge port of entry and was forced to return to the Centre.

“While Government continues to facilitate lawful repatriation and deportations, we have noted that scores of people continue to arrive across various centers to take advantage of the repatriation process.

“These uncoordinated arrivals are putting a strain on our local communities who reside in the proximity of these centers, and they pose significant risks of health hazards and outbreaks.

“In this regard, we have put emergency measures to respond to these spontaneous arrivals and have asked our local authorities to ensure an orderly management of this situation.”

Kubayi said there is a notable decline in the number of repatriations from a peak of 4850 on 5 July to 1139 on 11 July.

World.title: Infant injured in WC mass shooting
World.content:
MALMESBURY - Six adults and an infant were injured in a mass shooting and were admitted to hospital for medical treatment.

The infant was subsequently transferred to Red Cross War Memorial Children’s Hospital. The injured victims are reported to be in a stable condition.

Two people were killed in the shooting.

Detectives are investigating two counts of murder and seven counts of attempted murder following a shooting incident in Wesbank during the early hours of Sunday, 12 July 2026.

Police members responded to the complaint at approximately 04:40 in Godetia Street, Wesbank, where they found the bodies of a 22-year-old man and a 21-year-old woman who had sustained fatal gunshot wounds.

Colonel Andrè Traut said preliminary investigations indicate that a group of people was gathered outside a residence when unknown suspects opened fire on them.

“Evidence recovered at the scene suggests that more than one assailant may have been involved in the attack.

“The motive for the shooting is yet to be established and forms part of the ongoing investigation. The possibility that the incident may be gang-related is being investigated.

In the wake of the incident, policing in the area has been reinforced to prevent further violence and any possible retaliatory attacks.

No arrests have been made and the suspects are yet to be identified.

Anyone with information that could assist the investigation is kindly requested to contact Crime Stop on 08600 10111 or submit information anonymously via the MySAPS mobile application.

World.title: SAHRC calls for alcohol law reform
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The SA Human Rights Commission has welcomed the inquest findings that several individuals failed to act to prevent the Enyobeni tragedy.

The Commission’s Eileen Carter is calling on government to expedite alcohol law reforms.

“The World Health Organization has pointed towards South Africa being amongst the top 10 consumers of alcoholic beverages, and it certainly leads to a scourge of incidences that are preventable.

“We also found in our report that from a systemic failures point of view, the Department of Trade and Industry and the Department of Social Development have failed to progress legislation that is designed from South Africa's policies to prevent and address these issues.

“So, for more than 10 years, the liquor amendment bill as well as the Control of Marketing of Alcoholic Beverages bill have just been lying dormant and it hasn't been properly progressing through the structures yet.

“Now, as a result of this inquest outcome as well, the Commission will now be calling for meetings with the relevant ministers so that we can see where the holdup is in progressing these pieces of legislation that speak to protecting the rights not only of the youngsters who tragically died in this incident, but South Africa as a whole,” Carter said.

On 26 June 2026, a total of 21 young people were killed at Enyobeni Tavern. The youngest victim was 13 years old.

World.title: Oburu declares ODM won't field presidential candidate, endorses Ruto
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM party leader Oburu Oginga during funds drive at Chiga Catholic Church in Homa Bay Town Constituency on July 12, 2026. [James Omoro, Standard]

ODM leader Oburu Oginga has publicly declared that the party will not field a presidential candidate in the next General Election.

This statement is expected to end speculation in Nyanza over the party’s political direction.

Leaders including ODM Chairperson Gladys Wanga have been saying they had given Dr Oburu the mandate to negotiate with other political parties for a pre-election coalition agreement ahead of the polls.

This left many ODM supporters guessing whether the party would form a coalition with the United Opposition or President William Ruto's UDA party.

But Oburu has now settled the matter after saying consultations for a pre-election coalition agreement are complete, and ODM will support President Ruto’s re-election bid.

Speaking during a funds drive at Chiga Catholic Church in Homa Bay Town constituency, where he was accompanied by Interior Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo, the ODM leader said the party had scrutinised various political outfits and found that only Ruto was suitable for the presidency.

"I want to declare it official that ODM will not field a presidential candidate in next year's General Election. Instead, we are going to support President Ruto to be re-elected for a second term," Oburu said.

He argued that Ruto had shown them a good gesture by incorporating ODM members in government.

The Siaya Senator said it was only prudent that they reciprocate by supporting the President’s re-election bid.

"We didn't vote for this government but we were incorporated through the backdoor because Ruto loved us," Oburu said.

Oburu urged Nyanza residents to register as voters in large numbers to boost the region’s bargaining power.

"This time we are going to form the next government officially through the front door. But Ruto is going to ask me the number of voters from my backyard. Register as voters in large numbers to give us strength," he said.

PS Omollo urged Nyanza residents to support President Ruto to benefit from development projects.

He said that Ruto's administration had initiated development projects in Nyanza, a region which had been marginalised by previous regimes.

Dr Omollo defended Ruto saying he had enhanced regional balance in development.

"Many administrations in this country had discriminated against Nyanza. But today there's development in Nyanza as well as other regions in the country," he said.

The PS urged youths to shun politicians iniciting them to cause chaos.

"If you don't like any political leader, don't attend his meetings," Omollo said.

Homa Bay Town MP Peter Kaluma, who hosted the leaders, urged Nyanza residents to rally behind Oburu to ensure the community speaks in one voice.

"Our unity will give us a voice and this will help us in negotiations for power," Kaluma said.

Homa Bay Senator Moses Kajwang told Nyanza residents to shun tribal leaders.

"Let's avoid tribal leaders. Ruto has proved inclusivity by implementing development in our region," Kajwang said.

He hit out at Siaya Governor James Orengo for declaring himself ODM de facto leader.

"There is nothing like a de facto ODM leader. We have only one leader, Oburu Oginga," Kajwang said.

The Public Health PS Ouma Oluga urged residents to register for the Social Health Authority.

World.title: Why Linda Mwananchi leaders cancelled Ol Kalou tour
World.content:
Linda Mwanachi leaders led by Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna held a series of rallies in Kisii County. [Linda Mwanachi, X]

Unity within the Opposition appears to be under fresh strain after the Edwin Sifuna-led Linda Mwananchi Movement cancelled plans to hold rallies in Ol Kalou Constituency this weekend.

The Linda Mwananchi brigade will instead convene a meeting in Nyahururu Town on Sunday. Analysts argue that the former deputy president probably thinks Kangata is attempting to popularise Sifuna in his Mt Kenya stronghold.

World.title: Karua condemns convoy attack, blames police lapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

PLP leader Martha Karua. [Boniface Okendo, Standard]

People's Liberation Party (PLP) leader Martha Karua has condemned an attack on her convoy at Gatoto Primary School in Mukuru kwa Reuben, alleging police failed to provide security despite a High Court order.

In a statement on Friday, July 10, Karua said she had accompanied members of the Gatoto Primary School Board of Directors to oversee the implementation of a High Court judgment restoring the school's management to its lawful board.

She alleged that the High Court had directed the Officer Commanding Station (OCS) at Mukuru kwa Reuben Police Station to provide security for the exercise.

According to Karua, when the board members reported to the station, the OCS was unavailable while his deputy declined to deploy officers, saying only the OCS could authorise the deployment.

Karua said they proceeded to the school without a police escort, where they found the gates locked.

She claimed the situation turned chaotic shortly after members of the media arrived, with a group of people pelting vehicles belonging to board members with stones and forcing the convoy to leave the area.

Karua further alleged that one of the attackers smashed the rear windscreen of her vehicle using a rungu.

Condemning the incident, Martha Karua said it raised broader concerns about respect for court orders and the rule of law.

"Today's events are not merely about Gatoto Primary School. They raise a broader national question about whether Kenyans can continue to rely on public institutions to enforce court decisions impartially and protect those exercising their constitutional rights," she said.

Karua called for investigations into both the attack and the alleged failure by police to enforce the court order, urging authorities to hold those responsible accountable.

World.title: Registrar of Political Parties okays Sifuna's removal as ODM secretary general
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna. [File, Standard]

The removal of Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna as the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) Secretary-General has been formalised by the Office of the Registrar of Political Parties (ORPP).

In a letter, the registrar's office said that Sifuna’s removal process by the party’s National Executive Council complied with its constitution and the Political Parties Act.

"Upon review of the documents submitted by the party and the lack of response from Hon. Edwin Watenya Sifuna, we note that the removal of the party Secretary-General was in line with the Political Parties Act, Cap. 7D, and the ODM party constitution," the letter signed by ORPP Chief Executive Offier John Lorionokou reads.

He added that the office made the decision after considering communication on the ODM’s NEC powers to set up and determine issues of discipline within the party.

“The office has effected the change and updated the party records.”

Sifuna through his legal team challenged the ORPP decision.

In a letter, Senior Counsel Isaac Okero said that the move was a clear procedural irregularity and the changes should not be effected.

"Our client considers this action to be procedurally improper. Effecting changes to the party records violates the Political Parties Act, and our client will not hesitate to pursue the appropriate legal remedies," the letter by Okero says.

The battle for the SG’s post began on February 11, 2026, when an NEC meeting convened in Mombasa, passed a resolution to oust Sifuna replacing him with Busia Woman Representative Catherine Omanyo in acting capacity.

The Mombasa meeting was led by the then acting Party leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Odinga and other top leaders of the party.

Sifuna challenged his removal at the ODM party Disciplinary Committee and the Political Parties Disputes Tribunal.

At the ODM Disciplinary Committee Sifuna did not file a response to several allegations levelled against him which included contradicting the party’s position.

World.title: Kalonzo condemns police over their conduct during Saba Saba Day
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Police keep vigil as motorists are diverted along barricaded Parliament road, Nairobi during the Saba Saba Day commemorations on July 7,2026. [Elvis Ogina,Standard]

Wiper Patriotic Front Party Leader Kalonzo Musyoka condemned the National Police Service for turning its guns and batons on the citizens it exists to protect during the 36th Saba Saba Day.

Kalonzo said that Peaceful marchers were met with an excessive deployment of police officers, roadblocks and the deliberate closure of major roads, effectively curtailing the constitutional freedoms of movement, assembly and peaceful protest.

The Wiper Party Leader raised concerns that Plainclothes and masked officers forcibly seized young Kenyans from our streets into unmarked vehicles across the country while concealing their identities in blatant disregard of the rule of law and existing court orders.

“This is not policing, this is intimidation in service of a regime that fears its own people, even more disturbing is the growing pattern of police officers appearing to act alongside or provide protection to organised criminal gangs and militia groups that have terrorised innocent Kenyans in broad daylight,” said Kalonzo.

He pointed out that during the attacks on the Linda Mwananchi team in Kisii, at a hotel in Westlands, Nairobi and along Thika Road citizens were robbed and assaulted while law enforcement officers either stood by or failed to intervene such conduct gravely undermines public confidence in the National Police Service and has no place in a constitutional democracy.

Kalonzo reminded the National Police Service of its own motto: "Utumishi Kwa Wote — Service to All.” Not service to an individual or a political administration, but service to Kenya, to her Constitution, and to every Kenyan who calls this country home.

“Ask yourselves whose interests you defend when you arrest a mother marching for her missing son, or fire teargas at a student demanding accountability, I equally condemn the escalating attacks on opposition leaders, independent media and dissenting voices.

He said that the return of political intolerance under the Ruto regime is a dangerous attempt to drag Kenya back to the dark days of dictatorship that Saba Saba sought to end, a nation cannot claim to be democratic while intimidating political competitors, silencing the press and criminalising peaceful dissent.

Kalonzo said that these actions offend both the letter and the spirit of our Constitution calling for the immediate and unconditional release of every Kenyan arrested today while peacefully exercising their constitutional right to demonstrate.

“Peaceful protest is not a crime. It is a right expressly guaranteed under Article 37 of the Constitution, and no Kenyan should be detained for exercising that right, I also demand for immediate disciplinary action against all security agencies for their actions or inaction that has led to the violation of Kenyans constitutional rights,” said Kalonzo.

He said that when they form the next Government after the August 10, 2027 General Elections, we will deliver comprehensive police reform they will ensure every abduction and every death in custody is independently investigated and those responsible held fully accountable.

Kalonzo said when they get to power they will end the use of unmarked vehicles and unidentified officers against civilians and build a Police Service that answers to the Constitution, not to political power.

World.title: Kenya Kwanza leaders tell Uhuru to stay out of politics, act like a statesman
World.content:
Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka addresses residents during the Kimilili Women and Youth Economic Empowerment Forum at St John's Miruri Primary School on July 5, 2026. [Jackline Inyanji, Standard]

Kenya Kwanza leaders led by Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka, President’s aide Farouk Kibet and Taveta MP John Bwire, have called on former President Uhuru Kenyatta to uphold the dignity of the office he served and act like a statesman.

They hit out at the Linda Mwananchi leaders who attended the funeral of the brother of Bumula MP Jack Wamboka, claiming that the group is being used by former President Kenyatta.

World.title: Trump surprises Zelensky with public promise on Patriots – but the missiles may not come soon enough
World.content:
US President Donald Trump’s promise to allow Ukraine to manufacture Patriot interceptors has given a glimmer of hope to millions of Ukrainians terrorized by Russia’s deadly ballistic missiles strikes.

Speaking on the sidelines of the NATO summit in Turkey, Trump said a “little birdie told me … that we’ll give them the right to make Patriots.”

The announcement came as a surprise, even though Ukraine has been working on the issue for years, and there were some indications a deal could be close. Sat next to Trump, President Volodymyr Zelensky at times looked like he almost couldn’t believe his luck. The two men share a rocky relationship and the flareup in the war in Iran appeared to have put Trump into a foul mood just before his meeting with Zelensky.

Trump’s language was rather vague, and he admitted that he had not yet discussed the issue with the US companies manufacturing the Patriots – Lockheed Martin and Raytheon. They have not commented on it.

Zelensky said that getting production started would eventually allow Ukraine to produce enough interceptors for its needs as well as those of its allies.

Ukraine has always faced a tight supply of Patriot missiles, the only weapon that can take down some of Russia’s most advanced ballistic missiles. But the shortage has become critical in recent weeks – and the results have been devastating.

Russian attacks killed at least 59 people in Kyiv area in just the past week – with one massive aerial strike claiming 31 lives on Thursday and another killing 28 on Monday. More than 200 people were injured.

It is likely that many of these deaths could have been prevented if Kyiv had sufficient supplies of the interceptors.

Ukraine has become a master in defending its skies against Russian aerial attacks, using a combination of smart home-grown technology, Western-supplied weapons and scrappy military tactics that includes mobile units of soldiers and volunteers repurposing weapons meant for other uses to shoot down drones and missiles.

US President Donald Trump meets with Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky during the NATO Summit on July 8, 2026 in Ankara, Turkey. Win McNamee/Getty Images

Analysis of Ukrainian Air Force data shows that Ukraine is regularly shooting down 90% of Russian drones and cruise missiles. Ballistic missiles, however, are another beast, with two-thirds of those regularly getting through.

The shortage of Patriots has created even a bigger hole in the system. Ukraine’s military said on Wednesday that it failed to shoot down any of the Russian ballistic missiles fired at it overnight into Wednesday.

This is because ballistic missiles follow a curved trajectory that takes them out of the Earth’s atmosphere, before plunging back into the atmosphere and onto its target. They travel at extremely high speeds, which makes them very difficult to intercept – and Russia is currently firing as many as 100 such missiles every month.

Ukrainian servicemen walk past a Patriot air defense system at an undisclosed area on August 4, 2024. Sergei Supinsky/AFP/Getty Images/File

What makes Patriots so special?

The Patriots, short for Phased Array Tracking Radar for Intercept on Target, are the US Army’s key missile defense system.

It is the most advanced system available, and the price tag reflects that. With the complete setup of launchers, radars and interceptor missiles, each battery costs more than $1 billion, with a single interceptor costing up to $4 million, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

The technology behind the system is a closely guarded secret and currently, Japan and Germany are the only countries with licenses to co-produce Patriots domestically. The complexity of the weapon makes the production of the latest interceptor missiles difficult – only 600 are produced every year, according to the US Department of Defense.

The recent conflict between the US and Iran has put extra pressure on already stretched supplies, and Zelensky said getting production started in his country would eventually allow it to produce enough interceptors for the needs of itself and its allies.

Ukraine is believed to have at least seven Patriot systems: three that were supplied by the US; three from Germany; and at least one from a group of European allies.

While getting the license would be a major development for Kyiv, it would not do much in the short term. Getting production underway could take months but the country needs the defenses now. On Thursday, Kyiv said it had asked nearly 40 countries to provide Ukraine with missiles from their existing stocks as soon as possible, “in exchange for future deliveries already contracted for Ukraine.”

Securing the licenses would be a major boost for Kyiv, which is why Russia is watching any developments around the Patriots closely. Moscow has made no secret of targeting the systems in Ukraine and has warned Kyiv’s allies against supplying them.

Speaking to reporters during his daily briefing on Thursday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov downplayed the Patriot license promise as a major shift in the war, pointing to what he called a “certain ambivalence” and “duality” in Trump‘s position.

World.title: Iranian foreign minister holds phone call with Pakistani counterpart
World.content:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held a phone call with his Pakistani counterpart Mohammad Ishaq Dar on Sunday as tensions flared between Tehran and Washington.

“Both leaders exchanged views on the evolving regional situation,” according to a readout from Pakistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It added they agreed to remain in close contact.

Pakistan is a key mediator in negotiations between the US and Iran.

Araghchi traveled to Muscat on Saturday for a meeting with his Omani counterpart. According to a source, Oman has drafted a proposal to manage traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, a key sticking point in the conflict.

Mediators have been pushing to revive diplomacy between the US and Iran as they traded fire this week. The leaders of both countries also issued public threats this weekend.

And on Sunday, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf appeared to threaten the US on social media. Posting an excerpt of their 14-point agreement signed in June, he wrote: “The era of one-sided deals is OVER. We told you: keep your word or pay the price.”

World.title: Hormuz stalemate won’t change unless one side blinks
World.content:
By now the pattern is familiar. An Iranian drone strikes a ship transiting the Strait of Hormuz without Tehran’s consent. The United States responds with air strikes against targets on the Iranian coast. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps retaliates with missile and drone attacks on the US’ Gulf allies, claiming it is targeting American military facilities.

This sequence occurs even as Qatari and Pakistani mediators try to keep the diplomatic track alive. Qatar was targeted in the latest Iranian barrage. So was Oman, which on Saturday hosted Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi for talks on navigation through the strait.

Hormuz offers Iran critical leverage. So long as it can limit passage through the strait, either through force or the threat of force, it can have an impact on global energy flows.

“This strategic waterway is one of the country’s deterrent assets,” said Mohsen Rezaei, military adviser to Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, on Sunday.

Senior US officials said that Iranian negotiators had blamed an “errant part” of Iran’s system for attacks on three ships last week.

That “allows the regime to sustain talks and attempt to reap potential economic benefits while the IRGC continues to enforce Iran’s control over the strait,” the Washington-based Institute for the Study of War (ISW) said Saturday.

But “the differences between the negotiators and the IRGC are one of immediate tactical means – negotiations or military action – not strategic ends,” ISW added.

The US demands Iran publicly acknowledge that the strait is open to all commercial traffic and end attacks on vessels. Tehran has rejected any return to the pre-war situation, when there was unfettered freedom of navigation.

Squaring that circle seems beyond either side at present.

“US operations seem focused on imposing costs on Iran rather than fundamentally changing the strategic reality in the strait,” wrote Israeli analyst Danny Citrinowicz Sunday.

It’s difficult to see maritime traffic returning to normal unless “either Iran and Oman reach an arrangement that reduces tensions over navigation, or the United States abandons its effort to route tankers through the southern channel over Iran’s objections,” Citrinowicz said on X.

World.title: Did Cristiano Ronaldo cry? The hotly debated answer cost millions of dollars
World.content:
This World Cup, a bunch of people decided to gamble millions on whether soccer superstar Cristiano Ronaldo would cry during a match.

The bet, which happened on Polymarket, isn’t weird for the wild world of prediction markets. Like whether aliens will be announced by the US government, whether a coup attempt will take place in Russia — even whether the earth is flat. (One trader lost $915 betting against the earth’s sphericity).

So traders looking to get an edge began closely examining Ronaldo’s long, storied career for evidence of crying. There were tears of despair, like from Portugal’s heartbreaking 2022 World Cup loss, in which he kneeled on the grass while weeping. There was also a record of happy tears, like this year, when he helped his club secure the Saudi title for the first time during his tenure.

This week, the odds had settled at around 70% favoring tears.

Monday’s match was to be Ronaldo’s last of this World Cup, ending in heartbreak for the 41-year-old soccer legend, with Portugal falling to Spain 1-0. It could be his final World Cup match ever.

So did he cry or what?

“You see Ronaldo here, obviously very emotional,” a FOX broadcaster remarked as the Portuguese legend wiped his face and walked off the pitch.

But exactly how emotional was he? The harder they looked, the less everyone agreed. Then the investigations began.

Enhance!

Ronaldo looks dejected after the match as Portugal are eliminated from the World Cup. Jerome Miron/Imagn Images

After the match, users on Polymarket’s Discord channel began downloading and scrutinizing zoomed-in photos of Ronaldo’s scrunched face. The odds shot up and down as new evidence came in.

Related article 

Arrows were added pointing to potential tears on Ronaldo’s right eye and nose. Newly found video angles were scrutinized frame-by-frame.

“Only sweat and glistening skin,” said one user in the “no-crying” camp. “Yes, he is tearing up, fighting it. But clearly there are no tears.”

Another pointed to Ronaldo’s previous, wetter sobs, listing three “good examples” of Ronaldo “clearly shedding tears in the past,” including Ronaldo’s acceptance speech for winning the 2013 Ballon D’Or during which falling liquid can clearly be seen on the right side of his cheek.

The historical record: Cristiano Ronaldo cries after receiving the trophy for the world player at the FIFA Ballon d’Or 2013 Gala in Zurich, Switzerland, January 13, 2014. Michael Probs/AP

But those in the pro-crying wing dismissed the so-called “sweat theory.”

“Yes, he cried, and we all know he cried,” one Discord user wrote. “It’s possible to draw this conclusion from the micro-expressions of sadness in the videos and photos.”

Some in the pro-crying camp pointed to articles and headlines as proof.

The BBC’s headline read “Ronaldo’s World Cup career ends in tears…,” while ESPN also included a sorrowful description: “A visibly emotional Ronaldo wiped tears from his eyes as he applauded the fans.”

“You cannot wipe tears that don’t exist,” the poster noted.

Crying foul

Ronaldo greets fans after losing the 2026 World Cup round of 16 football match between Portugal and Spain at the Dallas Stadium in Arlington on July 6. Thomas Coex/AFP/Getty Images

Polymarket’s procedures call for disputed markets to be adjudicated by the company’s internal markets team and then formally voted on by holders of the cryptocurrency UMA.

After the debate started brewing, Polymarket flagged the market for review, eventually making a determination: yes, they said. He cried.

“As of the time of this Clarification, there exists qualifying photographic and video evidence, taken on the field during the aftermath of the Portugal v. Spain game, depicting Cristiano Ronaldo crying, including visible tears on his face,” they wrote.

Polymarket did not, however, reveal which specific evidence they used to reach their decision.

With that final judgment, millions of dollars changed hands as the trade finalized.

“Where is evidence?,” raged one user on the market’s comment section.

“Did Gianni Infantino decide this?,” wrote another, referencing the controversy-prone FIFA head.

A source familiar with Polymarket’s process said that the crying is obviously debatable: “It is a total Rorschach test. It could go either way.”

The source told CNN that Polymarket’s markets team combed through evidence, including photos, video and news reports, but didn’t post them for fears that it could invite “hyperfixation” from users who might accuse them of being AI-manipulated and that it could potentially invite litigation.

Ron Yurko, Assistant Teaching Professor in the Department of Statistics and Data Science at Carnegie Mellon University and Director of the Carnegie Mellon Sports Analytics Center, described Polymarket’s failure to post the evidence as a sign of the “Wild West” regulatory environment for prediction markets.

“It’s actually pretty crazy they don’t offer any proof,” he said. “This is part of the lack of transparency around these markets. Which is why a regular person should be very cautious about participating in it.”

Polymarket declined to publicly comment on the evidence used to determine its outcome.

A professional opinion on crying

Dr. Ad Vingerhoets, a clinical psychologist and emeritus professor of Emotions and Wellbeing with the Department of Medical and Clinical Psychology of Tilburg University, who is a leading expert on crying with research focusing on “emotional tears,” said that the footage showed Ronaldo on the verge of crying but doing his best to hold back the tears.

“He’s clearly about to cry,” Dr. Vingerhoets said. “But he’s struggling.”

Dr. Vingerhoets opined that if you were to use the production of tears as the decisive criteria in determining if Ronaldo cried, “then the conclusion must be: no crying.”

But Dr. Vingerhoets still said that, by his own definition, he does consider it a cry.

“I can fully agree with the conclusion that, despite the absence of visible tears, what we see here is crying and the struggle to suppress it,” he said.

The post-truth betting era

Traditionally, resolving bets is a no-brainer.

The New York Knicks win by 10. Jalen Brunson puts up 31 points. Josh Hart snags ten rebounds. There’s not really much to dispute in a box score.

But prediction markets like Polymarket and Kalshi have opened the door for bets unthinkable in the past. (CNN has a partnership with Kalshi, using its data to interpret events; our journalists are prohibited from using all prediction markets.)

Not only is there a market on Polymarket for whether Jesus will return (which will resolve to ‘yes’ only “if The Second Coming of Jesus Christ occurs by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.”) — there’s also a secondary market on whether the odds of the Jesus returning market will exceed a certain percentage.

Because of the vast amount of money being thrown into these markets, semantic debates have exploded into financial ones.

Pedro Pascal, Karol G, Bad Bunny, Cardi B, Jessica Alba, Stephani Sosa and Alix Earle at Super Bowl LX on February 08, in Santa Clara, California. Christopher Polk/Billboard/Getty Images

Earlier this year, markets popped up on Polymarket and Kalshi over whether rapper Cardi B would “perform” at the Super Bowl halftime show. During Bad Bunny’s show, Cardi B made a cameo dancing alongside actors Jessica Alba and Pedro Pascal — but she did not sing. Her appearance led to extreme parsing of the phrase “performed.” Polymarket ended up marking its $5 million dollar market as “Yes,” while Kalshi partially refunded its users. At least one trader filed a complaint against Kalshi with federal regulators for the judgment, according to the New York Times.

“The more that they are allowed,” said Yurko, “the more we are going to see situations where it’s ambiguous — and outrage from people who are determined to be the winning bet.”

World.title: Egypt wins off the field, as World Cup heightens tourist appetite
World.content:
While millions around the world are focused on the pitch to follow the 2026 World Cup, Egypt is basking in gains that extend far beyond sports.

The national team’s journey has transformed into one of the biggest indirect promotional campaigns Egypt has enjoyed in recent years.

Qualifying for the Round of 16 wasn’t just an achievement that put the Pharaohs back on the global stage – it also opened the door to a new wave of international interest in Egypt as a tourist, cultural, and historical destination.

Discussions taking place on digital platforms, sports forums, and social media were filled with questions about traveling to Egypt, the costs of visiting, and the best tourist attractions to explore.

Tourism and media experts believe this is an exceptional opportunity that should be quickly seized to transform the sporting momentum into real economic and tourism returns that will support the Egyptian tourism sector in the coming years.

Media expert Ahmed Elwy said that major sporting events are no longer merely competitions on the field, but have become global platforms for shaping a nation’s image and enhancing its presence on the international stage.

He added that the millions of viewers who followed the Egyptian national team’s matches during the World Cup were not only watching the players, but also learning about Egyptian culture and history.

Tremendous value

Elwy explained that this represents tremendous media value that is difficult to achieve through traditional advertising campaigns, regardless of their budgets.

He explained that the team’s success in reaching the knockout stages contributed to increasing the frequency with which Egypt’s name is mentioned in international media and on social media platforms.

Elwy pointed out that many foreign fans began searching for information about the country represented by this stellar team.

He said that the real media gains begin after the matches conclude, as this global interest can be leveraged to produce tourism and digital content targeting international markets.

This content should link the sporting achievement with Egyptian tourist destinations, thus reinforcing Egypt’s image as a modern nation with a rich history, civilization, and unique tourist attractions, Elwy explained.

International experience has proven that sports are one of the most important tools of soft power, Elwy noted, citing the tourism and economic gains achieved by many countries after hosting major tournaments or achieving remarkable sporting accomplishments.

A golden opportunity

Tourism expert Sayed Nofal said that the national team’s performance in the World Cup represents a golden opportunity for the Egyptian tourism sector, especially given the increased global interest in Egypt in recent weeks.

He added that every match played by the Egyptian team in front of hundreds of millions of viewers worldwide served as a free advertising opportunity for Egypt, emphasizing that the marketing value of this media exposure sometimes exceeds the cost of massive promotional campaigns implemented by many countries.

Nofal explained that initial indicators reveal a clear increase in curiosity among many foreign fans to learn more about Egypt, whether regarding tourist destinations, travel costs, or the best times to visit.

He noted that the growing interest is not limited to traditional markets that send tourists to Egypt, but extends to new markets in North America, Latin America, and parts of Europe—markets with significant growth potential in the coming years.

Nofal indicated that what is needed at this stage is the launch of rapid digital campaigns targeting the audiences who followed the national team’s matches, along with offering diverse tourism packages and programs that combine cultural, beach, and leisure tourism.

What is needed now is the launch of rapid digital campaigns targeting the fans who followed the national team’s matches, along with offering diverse tourism packages and programs that combine cultural, beach, and leisure tourism, he added.

Bringing attention back to the homeland

Observers believe that one of the most important indirect results of Egypt’s successful participation in the World Cup is the shift in conversation from the national team to the country itself.

Fans searching for information about the Egyptian national team, its players, or their hometowns find themselves confronted with a history spanning thousands of years, with the pyramids, the Grand Egyptian Museum, the Nile River, Red Sea resorts, North Coast cities and more to enjoy.

This rapid digital journey from football to tourism represents, in itself, a significant marketing opportunity, especially in an era where search engines and social media platforms have become the primary gateways to travel decisions.

Experts agree that sporting success alone is insufficient for achieving sustainable gains, and comprehensive plan is needed to capitalize on the public and media momentum generated during the tournament.

This should plan includes strengthening digital campaigns targeting specific markets, collaborating with influencers and sports and tourism content creators, and producing promotional materials that connect sporting achievements with Egypt’s cultural identity.

The stories and personal experiences of Egyptian players can be leveraged to present a more relatable image to international audiences, enhancing the appeal of Egypt as a tourist destination.

True success isn’t measured solely by the number of goals or match results, but also by the level of global attention a country has garnered and the economic and tourism opportunities that can arise from this interest.

Experience proves once again that sports and tourism are two sides of the same coin, and that success on the pitch can become a bridge extending from international audiences to Egypt’s beaches, historical sites, and tourist cities, bringing the country gains that far exceed the confines of a single match.

World.title: Naguib Sawiris boosts funding for Egypt’s pyramids facilities development
World.content:
Orascom Pyramids Entertainment, owned by billionaire Naguib Sawiris, is increasing its investment in ancient Egyptian archaeological sites by a third, betting on sporting events and pop concerts by stars like Shakira to help propel tourism to new heights.

The new investment, totaling approximately US$ 10 million, will fund additions including a fleet of 30 multi-stop electric buses for tours and a lightweight steel outdoor arena with a capacity of up to 15,000 spectators, Asharq Business reported CEO Amr Gazzarin as saying.

Orascom’s Contract

Orascom Pyramids Entertainment (OPE), has a 10-year contract with the government to develop the visitor experience at these colossal, 4,000-year-old monuments.

This concession, which saw the launch of new services worth $30 million in the spring of 2025, has made the company one of the key players in the North African country’s record-breaking tourism growth.

Egypt welcomed nearly 19 million visitors last year, second only to Morocco on the continent.

Tourism Minister Sherif Fathy says a record 20 million is possible in 2026, with nine million already recorded in the first six months.

This demonstrates the resilience of a vital source of foreign currency and employment in Egypt, despite nearly three years of conflict in the wider Arab world.

The government receives all revenue from ticket sales to the pyramids, while OPE earns income from leasing five sites on the plateau to event organizers, as well as from VIP tours and sponsorship deals.

The company also leases out locations for shops and owns some restaurants there.

Four million dollars in targeted revenue

The Pyramids attracted approximately 2.5 million visitors annually before the development project began.

By hosting major events, OPE aims to generate revenue of up to LE 200 million, or $4.1 million in 2026 and break even next year, according to Gazzarin.

Colombian superstar Shakira is scheduled to perform at the Pyramids in November, following in the footsteps of bands like the Red Hot Chili Peppers and the Black Eyed Peas who have performed at the pyramids over the past decade.

The company hopes to organize future events similar to the boxing match featuring Ukrainian heavyweight Oleksandr Usyk in May, Gazzarin added.

The company is considering options for purchasing new buses from Nasr Automotive Manufacturing Company, according to Gazzarin.

The Egyptian state-owned company recently signed an agreement with China’s FAW Group to locally manufacture a range of vehicles under the Nasr brand.

Another subsidiary of Orascom Investment Holding signed LE963 million financing agreement with Commercial International Bank last year to fund the redevelopment of the sound and light shows at the Giza Pyramids and surrounding areas.

World.title: Egypt, Jordan to hold talks on gas cooperation
World.content:
Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi will embark on a one-day visit to Amman, Jordan on Sunday. He will meet with Jordan’s Minister of Energy and Mineral Resources Saleh al-Kharabsheh to discuss ways to improve cooperation in the gas sector.

The talks will cover joint cooperation efforts between Egypt and Jordan, ways to support integration in the gas sector and how to strengthen the exchange of expertise between both sides.

This visit reflects the friendly relations and ongoing coordination between Cairo and Amman, especially in the gas sector, which is a key area of cooperation for both countries.

World.title: Egypt, Congo discuss boosting military, security cooperation
World.content:
Defense Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ashraf Salem Zaher met with Congolese Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defense and Veterans Affairs Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita to discuss regional developments and ways to enhance military and security cooperation between the two countries.

The Congolese Defense Minister and his accompanying delegation were accorded an official reception at the Ministry of Defense General Secretariat, where military bands played the national anthems of both countries.

The talks covered regional and international developments and their impact on security and stability in Africa, as well as mechanisms to expand areas of joint military cooperation.

Zaher highlighted the strong Egyptian-Congolese relations and stressed the importance of continued coordination and joint efforts to strengthen cooperation in defense fields.

Muadiamvita praised Egypt’s support for African issues and expressed his keenness to further coordinate on matters of mutual interest.

The meeting was attended by the Armed Forces Chief of Staff Ahmed Khalifa and senior military officials from both countries.

World.title: Mwape laid to rest in Chingola
World.content:
Former Copper Queens coach Bruce Mwape was on Sunday afternoon interred at Chingola Central Cemetery following a funeral service at Nchanga Stadium.

‎

‎Mwape, 67, died on Thursday morning at Nchanga South Mine Hospital in Chingola after an illness.

‎

‎Football Association of Zambia President Keith Mweemba said the late coach’s legacy should inspire local coaches to take the national flag higher.

‎

‎Mweemba hailed Mwape for leading the Copper Queens to two Olympics and a World Cup, and challenged the team to win the WAFCON title in his honour.

‎

‎“To the football community, Coach Mwape was an icon who brought a lot of joy and respectability to the women’s game. Part of the unparalleled following that the women’s game is enjoying today is down to the work put in by Coach Mwape,” he said.

‎

‎“We know that a WAFCON trophy and World Cup qualification will be a befitting honour to Coach Mwape,” Mweemba added.

‎

‎Dignitaries present included Chipolopolo coach George Lwandamina, former Chingola Mayor Johnson Kang’ombe, National Sports Council of Zambia CEO Sombwa Musunsa, FAZ General Secretary Charles Chakatazya, and FAZ Exco members.

‎

‎Mwape coached the senior Zambia women’s team from 2018 to 2024. He took the Copper Queens to back-to-back Olympics in Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, and to a historic first FIFA Women’s World Cup in 2023.

‎

‎He also guided Zambia to a bronze medal at the 2022 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations in Morocco.

‎

‎At club level, the experienced trainer coached Nchanga Rangers, Roan United, Indeni and Konkola Mine Police.

He was also a former Nchanga player and won the 1998 Super League title with the club as assistant to Fordson Kabole.

‎

‎Mwape was named CAF Best Women’s National Coach in Africa in 2021.

World.title: Zambia holds Ethiopia to seal U-17 World Cup qualification ‎
World.content:
Zambia has qualified for the 2026 FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup after beating Ethiopia 3-2 on aggregate in the final round of qualifiers.

‎

‎The return leg played on Sunday in Addis Ababa finished 1-1, as Zambia built on the 2-1 victory from the first leg in Ndola.

‎

‎Precious Mwewa scored for Zambia while Mihiret Ayene was the scorer for the Ethiopians.

‎

‎This is the third consecutive qualification for Zambia, who will be making their fourth appearance at the global event to be hosted by Morocco later this year.

‎

‎Zambia captain Taonga Mubanga said Ethiopia were tough opponents.

‎

‎“Today’s game was very tough although we managed to score first and they later equalised. Ethiopia really wanted to win today,” Ms. Mubanga said.

‎

‎She hailed the milestone.

‎

‎“We are happy to qualify for the World Cup three times in a row. We want to go and do better at the World Cup and reach as far as the semifinals,” she said.

‎

‎“To our fans, thank you for the support and continue supporting us. We will continue making you happy.”

‎

‎The Copper Princesses played with black armbands in honour of former Copper Queens coach Bruce Mwape, who was buried today in Chingola.

World.title: Copper Princesses 90 minutes from World Cup
World.content:
Zambia is on the verge of qualifying for the 2026 FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup as the Copper Princesses face Ethiopia on Sunday in the decisive return leg of the final round.

The match is scheduled for 15h00 local time in Addis Ababa, 14h00 Zambian time, at the Abebe Bikila Stadium.

Zambia take a 2-1 advantage into the tie after the first leg played at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Ndola a week ago.

The Copper Princesses will be seeking a historic third consecutive appearance at the global showpiece to be hosted by Morocco later this year.

Assistant Coach Naomi Phiri said the team is in Addis Ababa to finish the job.

“We are here to finish what we started back home. The girls understand what is at stake and we are ready,” Phiri said.

Zambia has featured in the last two editions of the FIFA Under-17 Women’s World Cup and will be banking on that experience.

A draw or win will see them through, but a loss by more than one goal would end their campaign.

World.title: Changala accuses Hichilema of “total arrogance” over campaign conduct
World.content:
Changala accuses Hichilema of “total arrogance” over campaign conduct

Civil rights activist Brebner Changala has accused President Hakainde Hichilema and the United Party for National Development (UPND) of taking Zambians for granted, saying the ruling party cannot expect to win support by returning to rural communities only during election campaigns after what he described as years of unresolved economic hardships.

Commenting on Hichilema’s campaign message to rural voters ahead of next month’s general election, Changala said the conduct of the ruling party during the campaign reflected what he described as growing arrogance towards the electorate.

“It’s clear that any mistake Zambians make to bring these guys back will be the last nail put in a coffin. All the UPND and Mr Hakainde want is votes. And that is total arrogance Zambians have been treated with,” he said.

Changala further accused the President of resorting to divisive politics after observing what he claimed was increasing public support for opposition parties during the campaign.

“Upon realising how Zambians are flocking to opposition rallies, Hichilema has resorted to divisive tribalistic campaigns. I want to warn Zambians that they must not vote for a man who is using tribe to cling to power. Mr Hichilema is using tribal politics and Zambians must be careful with him,” he said.

The activist argued that many citizens had endured difficult economic conditions during the UPND administration, citing the high cost of living, what he described as a shrinking democratic space and growing pressure on ordinary Zambians.

“In the last five years, Zambians have seen the worst, high cost of living, shrunk democratic space and stifled citizenry,” he said.

Turning to agriculture, Changala questioned the President’s recent pledge that farmers would receive immediate payments for maize deliveries through the Food Reserve Agency, saying previous delays had eroded confidence among producers.

“I wonder how the President thinks Zambians can still buy his claims on fertiliser and delayed payment to farmers under FRA when farmers have suffered for years due to delayed payments and poor planning by FRA,” he said.

He also challenged the ruling party’s messaging on free education, arguing that the policy should not be presented as an achievement unique to the current administration because Hichilema himself benefited from free education during his own schooling.

“Hichilema and UPND cannot claim credit for free education when the Head of State himself is a product of free education,” Changala said.

The activist further accused the government of interfering in opposition politics through what he described as the use of restrictive laws and alleged that the Patriotic Front had been taken over by individuals aligned with the state.

“He has stolen the country’s biggest opposition party, the Patriotic Front, and handed it to some state-sponsored individuals,” he said.

World.title: Mundubile Urges Public Institutions To Remain Neutral ahead of August polls
World.content:
NRPUP presidential candidate Brian Mundubile has appealed to public institutions to remain neutral and allow Zambians to decide freely in next month’s general election, warning that reports of partisan conduct by some institutions risk undermining public confidence in the electoral process.

In a statement issued at the weekend, Mundubile directed his appeal to civil servants, teachers, council workers and other public officers, saying their constitutional responsibility was to serve all citizens impartially regardless of which political party is in power.

“My appeal is straightforward: let every public institution remain neutral and allow the Zambian people to decide freely at the ballot box,” he said.

He assured civil servants across the country that an NRPUP government would respect their professionalism and protect them from political interference, stressing that public officers should carry out their duties without being influenced by partisan interests.

“You have a constitutional duty to remain professional, impartial and to serve all Zambians without political influence,” Mundubile said.

He said the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity was committed to improving the welfare of civil servants, restoring professionalism in the public service and reducing political interference in government operations. He added that his administration would pursue reforms, including a debt swap arrangement aimed at strengthening local authorities and improving service delivery.

The opposition leader said the August 13 election should reflect the freely expressed will of the people rather than be influenced by fear, intimidation or the misuse of public institutions for partisan advantage.

Turning to his party’s campaign agenda, Mundubile said NRPUP remained focused on policies centred on job creation, support for farmers, youth empowerment, expanding opportunities in the mining sector, improving public services and building an economy that benefits all Zambians.

“Our campaign remains focused on practical solutions: creating jobs, supporting farmers, empowering young people, expanding opportunities in the mining sector, improving public services and building an economy that works for every Zambian. On 13 August, let us choose hope, unity and meaningful change,” he said before ending his remarks with a rallying call in Bemba.

His comments came as an editorial in one national newspaper urged civil servants to remain neutral and focus on their constitutional mandate of serving the public. The editorial cautioned that public officers who allow themselves to be drawn into partisan politics risk compromising their professional standing once elections are over and political leadership changes.

It argued that governments and politicians come and go, while the civil service remains a permanent institution that must continue serving citizens irrespective of the party in office.

Meanwhile, addressing supporters during a campaign rally in Chifunabuli over the weekend, Mundubile said his administration would govern the country based on Christian values, pledging to restore what he described as the principles enshrined in the Constitution.

“We want to govern this country using Christian values. To all Christian men and women, we assure you that we are going to restore this country. We are going to reset this nation so that we can exist again as a Christian nation,” he said.

He also promised to depoliticise and professionalise the civil service through a merit-based recruitment system, saying competent and qualified public officers would be protected regardless of political affiliation.

“We will start by depoliticising the civil service. We will start by professionalising the civil service. The civil servants who are competent and qualified will be protected. We will restore our democracy and values. We will uphold our principles and values enshrined in our Constitution,” he said.

Mundubile said reforming the civil service formed part of a broader programme to improve governance, arguing that policy changes alone would not succeed unless senior public positions were filled on merit rather than political loyalty.

“We believe that policy reforms are not enough without state professionals being appointed to top positions simply because they are cadres. This negatively impacts leadership and affects the people. We are going to reform the civil service, and as long as you are qualified, you should be very comfortable,” he said.

The NRPUP leader also pledged to improve conditions of service for teachers and other public workers by increasing housing allowances and expanding investment in the education sector. He said his government would build more classrooms to accommodate growing enrolment under free education, recruit more teachers and construct additional staff houses in phases.

“In terms of free education, while we focus on school-going children, we will not forget about our teachers. We love and appreciate all our teachers; without you, we wouldn’t be where we are today. As we support school-going children, we will also ensure that teachers are respected and valued. We plan to build houses for teachers in phases, increase the number of classrooms and improve housing allowances to help teachers access decent accommodation,” he said.

World.title: “Same Thieves” who have only changed their name – Hichilema
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has told voters in Luangwa, Rufunsa and Chongwe not to “spoil” their votes on independent candidates, telling supporters that the ruling party needs five million votes to secure a stronger mandate than it won in 2021.

Addressing back-to-back rallies on Saturday, Hichilema described NRPUP leader Brian Mundubile and his running mate Makebi Zulu as figures from the former Patriotic Front who have simply regrouped under a new alliance name.

“Those who have come under new alliances, we know them. They have just changed their name. Do they become different? They are the same. The MP who was here is the same MP who was there in PF, now using a different party. They are the same crocodiles,” he said.

The Head of State urged supporters to vote with their heads rather than their stomachs, drawing a lengthy analogy between short-term hunger and long-term judgment.

“Vote using your brain, not using your stomach. The stomach feels hunger every day, but the head knows today, tomorrow, next month and next year. The stomach only knows that hour it is hungry, so when voting, use wisdom,” Hichilema said.

He said when a person is hungry they could even beat a child, but after eating they forget, while the head never forgets where a nation has come from. He referenced the debt burden Zambia inherited from the previous administration, asking supporters to weigh who was better between a leader who accumulated debt and one who worked to pay it back.

Turning to scripture, Hichilema likened returning to the former ruling party to the Israelites who, having been freed from slavery in Egypt by Moses, complained and longed to return.

“You have gone out of slavery and you are going to the promised land, then you want to go back to slavery? Can you go back? You go forward. On August 13, we are going forward,” he said.

The President also cautioned supporters against fielding or backing independent candidates, insisting that UPND was contesting a single candidate for each elective position in every constituency.

“I do not want anyone to go independent. There is only one position for UPND, that’s it. There is only one candidate for mayor, and one candidate for MP under UPND, and there is only one UPND symbol, the hand. Do not waste your vote on independents,” he said.

He questioned why he would field candidates under the UPND banner and then turn around to support independent contestants standing against them, asking supporters whether that would make sense.

Hichilema also dismissed suggestions that the opposition could win Lusaka, saying residents of the capital, together with those in Copperbelt, North-Western, Western and Central provinces, had already resolved to back the ruling party. He pointed to the turnout at a rally in Sinda the previous day as evidence of continued support, asking the crowd whether they had seen the numbers that gathered there.

On agriculture, the President said he wanted an end to farmers queuing for payment after delivering maize to the Food Reserve Agency, pledging that payments would instead be processed immediately through mobile money.

He also said he wanted to end situations where farmers shared limited Farmer Input Support Programme fertiliser and seed in tins or small measures, pledging to increase the number of FISP beneficiaries so that more farmers receive full allocations.

Hichilema further said the floor price for maize would be announced promptly once deliveries to the Food Reserve Agency begin, so that farmers are not left waiting.

Both Mundubile and Zulu had not responded directly to Hichilema’s “same thieves” characterisation by the time of publication. Campaigning continues this week as candidates make their final push across the provinces ahead of the August 13 general election.

World.title: ECZ Says Law Does Not Address Withdrawal of Running Mates Before Elections
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) says the country’s electoral laws do not provide for the withdrawal of a presidential running mate before a general election.

The matter has come into focus following the withdrawal of Organised People’s Party (OPP) running mate Andyford Banda and Citizens First running mate Moses Mawere, leaving presidential candidates Brian Mushimba and Harry Kalaba without running mates ahead of the August 13 General Election.

Speaking in an interview, ECZ Corporate Affairs Manager Patricia Luhanga said the resignation or withdrawal of a running mate does not invalidate a presidential candidate’s nomination or affect the electoral process.

Luhanga explained that while the law does not specifically address such a scenario, a presidential candidate remains validly nominated even after the withdrawal of a running mate.

She added that if such a candidate were elected President, a solution could be found after the election, including the appointment of another vice president in accordance with the law.

Meanwhile, ECZ Chairperson Mwangala Zaloumis said the Constitution only provides guidance on what happens if a Vice President vacates office after a presidential election and not when a running mate withdraws before polling day.

Zaloumis said the withdrawal of a running mate does not invalidate a presidential candidature because the law is silent on the matter.

She noted that the situation has exposed a gap in the country’s electoral legal framework, describing it as a legislative lacuna that may require future legal reforms.

World.title: HH assures Chongwe residents improved water supply
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has assured residents of Chongwe district that the government is committed to improving water supply in the area as part of its continued efforts to enhance access to essential services.

Speaking during a community engagement in Chongwe, President Hichilema urged residents to vote for the United Party for National Development (UPND) in the August 13 elections, to enable the party to continue implementing development programmes across the country.

The President said the government has recorded significant achievements since assuming office, citing free education, increased Constituency Development Funds (CDF) allocations and expanded infrastructure development as some of the notable milestones.

“We are asking the people of Chongwe to support the UPND because of the massive development that Zambia has experienced under this administration, including the introduction of free education,” President Hichilema said.

He further urged Zambians to safeguard the peace and stability the country is currently enjoying, adding that the government remains committed to promoting unity and rejecting violence.

President Hichilema also advised voters against electing independent candidates, saying they may not effectively support the implementation of government programmes.

On agriculture, the President assured farmers that the Food Reserve Agency (FRA) would soon announce this year’s maize purchase price and that farmers will be paid promptly after delivering their produce.

Chongwe East Aspiring Parliamentary Candidate Sylvia Masebo highlighted the achievements recorded under the UPND administration, particularly through the implementation of Constituency Development Funds (CDF) projects.

Ms Masebo thanked President Hichilema for visiting Chongwe East Constituency and reaffirmed the party’s commitment to improving the welfare of residents.

The President also assured residents that the government will continue creating employment opportunities for young people through various economic empowerment and development programmes.
